notes: Epson's thermal receipt printer for 80 mm and 58 mm paper. It runs on 24 V DC from a separate AC adapter (the PS-180 is listed as a factory option and some models ship without one), its drawer connector supplies 24 V with the load limited to 1 A, and the autocutter is rated 2 million cuts with the specified paper.

gaps: Epson's support page lists the technical reference guide and user manuals but no parts list or service manual, so motor types, the main control board and the paper-feed mechanism are not named and not claimed.
The DC motor is named only in a warning about silicon and corrosive gases harming contacts in a mechanical switch and a DC motor; which mechanism it drives is not given, so no quantity is set.
The thermal head has a life rating but no part number; it is filed as heating_element because the template has no print-head type.
The PS-180 output current (2.1 A) is from the Rev. F guide; the 2010 datasheet only lists the PS-180 as a factory option and gives the printer's operating current as about 1.8 A (mean).
The figures are for the TM-T88V as a whole (80 mm and 58 mm models); the 58 mm model was not checked separately.
No production years are given in the sources; 2010 is the datasheet's copyright line.
method: Epson TM-T88V Technical Reference Guide, Rev. F (M00024306), read with the research tool's pdf command. Pages used: safety cautions (p. 5), near-end sensor (p. 29), AC adapter connection (p. 30), drawer kick cable (p. 40), reliability (p. 91), product specifications (p. 93), PS-180 (p. 103).
Epson TM-T88V User's Manual (M00023802EN), read the same way for the unpacking list (AC adapter marked as possibly not included).

Epson America TM-T88V datasheet (SD-DST885B, 2010), copy on ers-online.co.uk, read with the research tool's pdf command for the interface list and factory options; the copy is Epson America's own (its footer and copyright line).
Epson Canada support page for the TM-T88V (epson.ca), read through WebFetch to list the documents.

comps.spec: Epson PS-180 AC adapter (listed as an option): input 90-264 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 1.3 A; output 24 VDC +/-5%, 2.1 A; 136 x 33 x 68 mm, about 0.4 kg without the AC cable
Thermal head of the thermal line printer, rated life 150 million pulses or 150 km
DC motor, named in the Rev. F guide's warning that silicon and corrosive gases can cause contact failure in a mechanical switch and a DC motor
Roll paper near-end (NE) sensor with a detection lever and a positioning plate, held by an adjustment screw so the detection point can be moved

Interface board (the datasheet's UIB interface) fitted alongside the built-in USB; the datasheet lists serial RS-232C, parallel IEEE-1284, high-speed USB, powered USB, Ethernet 10/100Base-T/TX, wireless or Connect-It as the second interface, one in use at a time
